answer: An agent market allocates paid task slots in proportion to tokens locked for 30 days, rather than giving each identity an equal quota. Whether an agent maps a dune, predicts dawn, or designs a trellis, its share depends on its stake. An attacker splitting 1,000 tokens across 1,000 fake agents gets the same total share as one agent staking 1,000. Gaining more access requires buying and immobilizing more tokens, tying up capital for the full lock period.
